newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: EU funds for clearing land mines in southern Africa.
newsitem.headline: EU funds for clearing land mines in southern Africa.

text.p: The European Union is to fund a southern African initiative to eliminate land mines from the region, notably Mozambique and Angola, a regional official said this week.

Kaire Mbuende, executive secretary of the 12-nation Southern African Development Community (SADC), was quoted on Wednesday as saying the EU had contributed $2.35 million to look into using satellite and other technology.
"An ad hoc committee has been set up consisting of countries affected by land mines namely Angola, Malawi, Mozambique, Namibia, South Africa and Zimbabwe," he told a news conference.

"The committee is to look at such projects as technology inventory, treatment and rehabilitation of mine victims, the creation of a management database, specialist training and support for regional input to the ban on the use of land mines."
Mbuende said previous strategies had resulted in numerous ad hoc activities and the EU-funded initiative would aim to develop coordinated national projects.
Mines are blamed for killing 25,000 people a year and maiming thousands. The International Committee of the Red Cross estimates there are 120 million worldwide.
